title: Second masked annotator for Tucker and Talbert: 2 of 4 genera recovered, both on the two most discussed folios
statement: Second annotator for P-L4-001, done blind to names but not to the literature. From the open PDF of Tucker and Talbert (2013, K-015) I extracted folio strings by script and printed only the folio ids (31 in the herbal range), removed the pilot's six (f5v, f6v, f9r, f24r, f25r, f32r), and drew six with Python random.Random(20261125).sample: f12v, f30v, f37v, f45r, f23v, f13r. f12v was dropped because folio 12 is missing from the manuscript. On the Yale scans (canvases 1006098, 1006119, 1006133, 1006147, 1006162, base https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/) I wrote down leaf, flower or fruit and root characters and a blind guess for each before printing any context. f13r: broad rounded palmately veined toothed leaves from a crown of cut petiole bases, a central spike of small blue-white bodies, a large red tuber; guess butterbur (Petasites) or a water-lily. f23v: one large radial blue flower with a ringed and fringed centre, small blue star flowers on side branches, toothed alternate leaves, branched red root; guess Passiflora, or Borago. f30v: alternate ovate serrate leaves, terminal hooked branches with rows of small pendant yellow bodies, horizontal rhizome; guess a scorpioid Boraginaceae (Heliotropium-like). f37v: paired wavy leaves, three dark-blue terminal bodies tipped red and white, branched root; no guess. f45r: three bluish stems from an orange rhizome, toothed lanceolate leaves, curled terminal spikes with two rows of small blue bodies; guess Boraginaceae or a fern. Reveal: f13r Petasites (P. frigidus var. palmatus), genus agrees; f23v Passiflora subgenus Decaloba, genus agrees; f30v Penthorum sedoides, family and genus disagree; f45r Salvia cacaliifolia, disagree; the f37v string refers to folio 37v of the Codex Osuna, not to a Voynich plant, and is excluded as the pilot excluded f9r. So 2 of 4 at genus, 0 of 4 at species (I named none). Pooled with the pilot (0 of 5) that is 2 of 9. The two agreements are not independent evidence: Passiflora on f23v and Petasites on f13r are among the most repeated identifications in the Voynich literature, I cannot exclude that I knew them, and the features I relied on (a corona-like ring; a palmate leaf from a crown of cut stalks) are the ones the literature points at. The two folios that are not famous were both missed. Neither agreement supports a New World origin by itself: the f23v flower is radial with a fringed ring, which also fits Nigella-like or composite heads drawn schematically, and Petasites has Old World species (P. hybridus, P. albus) that fit the same drawing at genus level. Next step, to make the test worth running: annotators must be screened for exposure (state beforehand which identifications they know) and the sample stratified to folios with no prior published identification other than Tucker and Talbert's; candidate lists for the multiple-choice stage must pair each proposed New World taxon with an Old World one of the same genus or family. No anchor follows: none of these folios has a label tied to the plant.
check: Repeat with an annotator who records exposure before seeing the scans, on folios outside the most discussed ones, and report agreement at family and genus with a matched Old World alternative for each proposed taxon.
